marks.gloss_en: שמע מינה -- since the baraita's fit-ruling is found only in the Egyptian myrtle, that myrtle is fit for the hoshana
Abaye: learn from it that this Egyptian myrtle is fit for the hoshana
ואימא הכי נמי! -- say it is indeed so: with a qualifying name it is not fit
עץ עבות אמר רחמנא, מכל מקום (= p_etz_avot_mikol_makom)
it teaches that, though it has a qualifying name, it is fit
most of its leaves dried and three twigs of moist leaves remained in it -- fit
version 1: the mishnah's psul applies only where the berries are in one place; in two or three places the myrtle is valid
כתיב הכא ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון (Vayikra 23:40), וכתיב התם ולקחתם אגודת אזוב (Shemot 12:22): מה להלן אגודה, אף כאן אגודה
ורבנן לית להו לקיחה לקיחה -- blocked in the Rabbis' framework only (= p_rabanan_lo_yalfi_lekicha)
and the Rabbis do not hold [the derivation of] 'taking' from 'taking'
ותפשוט ליה מהא דתנן -- the blood re-exposed obliges again, so there is no dichui with mitzvot and the berry that grew on Yom Tov restores the myrtle
the mishna: he covered it and it was uncovered -- exempt from covering
דרב פפא גופא מיבעיא ליה -- R' Yirmeya's question was about Rav Pappa's inference itself: perhaps it holds only lechumra, not lekula
ובפלוגתא דהני תנאי, דתניא: לולב בין אגוד בין שאינו אגוד כשר; רבי יהודה אומר אגוד כשר, שאינו אגוד פסול
or say: if we hold the lulav requires binding, all agree we learn lulav from sukkah; here they dispute whether the lulav requires binding
והוינן בה: כי חזר ונתגלה אמאי חייב לכסות? הואיל ואידחי אידחי! -- once [the obligation] was pushed aside, let it stay pushed aside
זאת אומרת אין דחוי אצל מצות (Rav Pappa's deny of p_yesh_dichui_bemitzvot)
אי רבי יהודה, כי לא אגדו אמאי כשר?
אי רבנן, מאי מצוה קא עביד?
a lulav -- it is a mitzva to bind it
Ulla bar Chinnana taught: its top was severed and a berry grew in it -- fit
R' Yirmeya: its top was severed on Yom Tov eve and the berry grew on Yom Tov -- is it fit?
if he transgressed and picked them -- unfit; the words of R' Elazar [son of R'] Tzadok
(entertained) they dispute this: the invalidator holds there is dichui with mitzvot, the validator that there is not
and here they dispute learning lulav from sukkah: one holds we learn lulav from sukkah, the other that we do not
